source.stem: Decide whether the following statements are correct. Mark “√” for correct answers and “×” for wrong answers. (1) Objects that can move must be living things.

hinge.title: Predict whether a nearby compass needle should deflect when electric current flows through a conductor.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: The needle deflects with the switch ON even if the circuit has a break.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: A stationary compass drives a steady current through a nearby closed wire loop without a cell.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: A current-carrying copper coil will not deflect the nearby compass; an iron coil will.

mx.name: mechanism_conflation
mx.teacher_note: The compass needle starts deflecting only after the current-carrying wire becomes hot.

intelligence.enrichment: An electric current flowing through a conductor produces a magnetic field around it; when the current stops, the magnetic field disappears. current flows in the conductor -> magnetic field forms around the conductor -> nearby compass needle deflects; current stops -> magnetic field disappears -> compass needle returns to its original direction The learner correctly applies this rule: An electric current flowing through a conductor produces a magnetic field around it; when the current stops, the magnetic field disappears. A compass needle moves only near a permanent magnet, so a wire connected to a cell should not move it.
